dedupe_keys.name: satellite constellation internet affordability and need

description: Meredith Rawls and colleagues publish a country-level comparison of estimated satellite-internet costs, GDP per capita and existing internet access. The October 2020 Zenodo deposit supplies StarlinkData_2018.csv under CC BY 4.0, with an R plotting repository separately licensed MIT. The analysis defines affordability as a service cost below ten percent of GDP per capita and unmet need using an internet-access threshold of 75 percent. These are study assumptions that can be varied in adoption or service-access simulations. The file name indicates a 2018 snapshot, but individual source vintages and country completeness remain unknown from the short documentation. Historical cost assumptions are not current service prices, and country averages do not describe household affordability. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this derived comparison. The CSV and plotting code were not downloaded or run.
